writeup: TIC 86880482 is a candidate eclipsing binary star detected through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The star shows a primary eclipse with a depth of 3.59% and an orbital period of 2.8284 days, producing a strong signal-to-noise ratio of 150.1 in the periodogram analysis. Pixel-level imaging confirms the eclipse signal originates from the target location, with a difference-imaging peak signal-to-noise of 25.6, though the centroid offset of 8.5 arcsec warrants attention. No secondary eclipse was detected. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a potentially new object. The pipeline's machine-learning classifier assigned a score of 0.54, indicating moderate confidence that this represents a real target. This candidate passed all data quality checks and merits further investigation.
